title: Nvidia, a maker of 3D graphics chips, goes public
what: Nvidia sold 3.5 million shares to the public on 22 January at 12 dollars, raising 42 million dollars. Founded in 1993, it designs graphics processors that draw three-dimensional images in personal computers, mainly for games, and has other companies manufacture them; its RIVA TNT chip of 1998 has made its name. Revenue for the nine months to October 1998 was 92.7 million dollars, with a small loss.
why: The listing beat. One of about seventy graphics start-ups of the 1990s, and one of only two to survive; 12 dollars at the IPO became more than 5,000 times its value by 2026, before dividends.

title: Nvidia announces the GeForce 256
what: On 31 August Nvidia announced the GeForce 256, which it calls the world's first graphics processing unit, or GPU: a single chip that also does the geometry and lighting calculations that until now were left to the computer's main processor. It is due in October.
why: The product that made Nvidia the leader in PC graphics. The +40% month cannot be tied to the announcement, which came on the last day of the month (see Unexplained moves).

title: The GeForce sells, and Nvidia's revenue nearly triples
what: The GeForce 256 went on sale on 11 October and is in strong demand at higher prices than older chips. Nvidia's revenue for the first nine months of its financial year was 246.1 million dollars, 184% more than a year earlier, driven by its RIVA TNT2 chips and the new GeForce.
why: Explains the +56% month, assuming the quarterly results were published in November as usual; the release date is not in the sources read (figures from the 10-Q filed on 10 December).
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/0001012870-99-004592.txt (Nvidia 10-Q for the quarter to October 1999, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_256 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Microsoft picks Nvidia for the Xbox
what: On 5 March Nvidia agreed with Microsoft to develop and sell the graphics processors for Microsoft's planned games console, the Xbox, which Bill Gates presented on 10 March. Microsoft will pay Nvidia 200 million dollars in advance against future chip purchases.
why: The contract that made Nvidia a major supplier; +32% in the month on top of February's gain. It also took many of its best engineers away from PC chips.

title: Nvidia buys the assets of its old rival 3dfx
what: On 15 December Nvidia agreed to buy the technology and patents of 3dfx Interactive, the pioneer of 3D graphics cards for games in the mid-1990s, which has fallen behind.
why: The end of the graphics-chip wars of the 1990s; from now on Nvidia's only serious rival was ATI.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/0001012870-01-500581.txt (Nvidia 8-K on the 3dfx asset purchase, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia (read 2026-10-03)

title: Nvidia restates its accounts, and fights Microsoft over Xbox prices
what: On 29 April Nvidia announced that a review by its audit committee, begun at the request of the SEC in January, concluded that its accounts for 2000, 2001 and most of 2002 must be restated, mainly for the timing of costs. The same day it disclosed that Microsoft has taken a dispute over Xbox chip prices and volumes to binding arbitration.
why: The start of Nvidia's 2002 collapse (-87% from December 2001 to September 2002), as the accounting cloud, the Xbox dispute and a strong rival chip from ATI came together.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/0001012870-02-002921.txt (Nvidia 10-Q/A for the quarter to April 2002, read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000095016802001118/d8k.htm (read 2026-10-03)

title: Nvidia unveils the GeForce FX
what: At the Comdex show in November Nvidia announced the GeForce FX, its new generation of graphics processors, built to compete with ATI's Radeon 9700. The first cards are due early next year. The stock market rose again in November.
why: +44% in the month on hopes for the new chip; in practice the FX arrived late and was less competitive than hoped.

title: New chips in production, market share up
what: On 8 May Nvidia reported revenue of 405 million dollars for the quarter to April, down from 583 million a year earlier, and a profit of 19.7 million. Chief executive Jen-Hsun Huang said its new GeForce FX family is in production across desktop, notebook and workstation chips and that its market share has risen; this month it also launched the faster FX 5900.
why: The +83% month came from relief that the worst was over after the 2002 collapse, not from strong numbers.

title: Nvidia will design the PlayStation 3's graphics
what: Nvidia announced that it will help Sony design the graphics processor for the PlayStation 3 games console.
why: A second console win after the Xbox, with Sony this time.

title: CUDA: graphics chips for general computing
what: Nvidia released the first version of CUDA, software that lets programmers use its graphics processors for general calculations that can be split into many parallel parts, not just for drawing images.
why: The long bet that made the AI boom Nvidia's: by 2025 Nvidia had more than 80% of the market for AI chips, largely because researchers built on CUDA. Nobody valued it in 2007.

title: Forbes names Nvidia company of the year
what: Forbes named Nvidia its company of the year for 2007, citing its achievements this year and over the past five years. Its shares have risen more than tenfold since the autumn of 2002.
why: The peak before the crisis; the shares fell more than 75% in 2008.

title: Faulty notebook chips and a profit warning
what: On 2 July Nvidia said it will take a charge of 150 to 200 million dollars to cover repairs and replacements of some older notebook graphics and chipset products that fail because of a weak packaging material. All products now shipping use a more robust material.
why: -39% in the month, the start of a brutal 2008 for Nvidia.

title: Intel will pay Nvidia 1.5 billion dollars
what: On 10 January Nvidia and Intel settled their legal fight with a patent cross-licence: Intel will pay Nvidia 1.5 billion dollars in licence fees over six years. Nvidia will not make chipsets for Intel's newer processors; it is building up its Tegra processors for mobile devices.
why: +55% in the month: a large, steady cash stream and the end of a damaging legal fight.

title: Tegra 4 and a handheld console
what: Nvidia unveiled its Tegra 4 processor for phones and tablets and the Nvidia Shield, a handheld games console running Android. Mobile chips are its bet on growth beyond PC graphics.
why: The shares went sideways from 2011 to 2015, before data centres changed everything.

title: Nvidia Drive: chips for cars
what: At the CES show Nvidia introduced Nvidia Drive, computing platforms for cars, including systems to help them drive themselves. Nvidia now concentrates on games, cars and mobile devices.
why: One of several new markets Nvidia tried for its GPUs in these years.

title: Pascal GPUs and growing demand for deep learning
what: On 6 May Nvidia unveiled its GeForce GTX 1080 and 1070 graphics cards on its new Pascal design. On 12 May it reported revenue of 1.30 billion dollars for the quarter, up 13%, with growth in games, professional graphics, data centres and cars; chief executive Jen-Hsun Huang said deep learning, a new computing model, is accelerating its growth.
why: +32% in the month; the start of the AI chapter. The shares more than tripled in 2016.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581016000243/q117pr.htm (Nvidia press release of 12 May 2016, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia (read 2026-10-03)

title: Nvidia gives OpenAI its first AI supercomputer
what: Nvidia gave the first DGX-1, a computer with eight of its graphics processors and software for deep learning, to OpenAI, a young AI research lab, to train larger models faster.
why: A small event at the time, symbolic in hindsight: OpenAI's ChatGPT set off the boom in Nvidia's data-centre chips six years later.

title: Record revenue, up 54%
what: On 10 November Nvidia reported record revenue of 2.00 billion dollars for the quarter to October, 54% more than a year earlier, and record profit margins, with demand from data centres for AI growing.
why: +30% in the month; the market began to price Nvidia as an AI company.

title: Artificial intelligence triples Nvidia's data-centre sales
what: Nvidia's graphics chips were made for video games, but they turn out to be ideal for training artificial intelligence. On 9 May the company reported quarterly sales of 1.94 billion dollars, 48% more than a year earlier; sales to data centres almost tripled, from 143 to 409 million dollars. The shares rose 38% in May.
why: The first time AI shows up in Nvidia numbers on this scale; the pattern of 2023, when the forecast stunned Wall Street, in miniature.

title: The crypto hangover
what: On 15 November Nvidia reported record data-centre revenue but said its near-term results reflect excess inventory of graphics cards left over after the cryptocurrency boom, when miners bought them in large numbers, and gave a weak forecast. Chief executive Jensen Huang said the problem will be corrected.
why: -22% in November, part of a fall of more than half from the September 2018 peak.

title: Nvidia buys Mellanox for 6.9 billion dollars
what: On 11 March Nvidia agreed to buy Mellanox Technologies, an Israeli maker of high-speed networking equipment for data centres and supercomputers, for 6.9 billion dollars.
why: Gave Nvidia the networking that ties thousands of GPUs together into one AI computer, a key part of its later dominance.

title: Nvidia agrees to buy Arm for 40 billion dollars
what: On 13 September Nvidia agreed to buy Arm, the British designer of the processors in almost all smartphones, from SoftBank for 40 billion dollars, subject to approval by regulators; SoftBank would keep about 10% of Nvidia.
why: It would have been the largest chip deal in history; regulators blocked it.

title: Nvidia forecasts 11 billion dollars and stuns Wall Street
what: On 24 May Nvidia reported record data-centre revenue of 4.28 billion dollars and forecast revenue of 11.0 billion dollars for the next quarter, about half more than in the quarter just ended. Jensen Huang said a trillion dollars of data-centre equipment will shift to accelerated computing as companies race to use generative AI, and that Nvidia is sharply increasing supply. Quarterly sales were 7.19 billion dollars, and the forecast was far above what analysts expected.
why: +36% in the month; the moment the AI boom showed up in a forecast. Nvidia passed a trillion dollars in market value in 2023.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581023000087/q1fy24pr.htm (Nvidia press release of 24 May 2023, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia (read 2026-10-03); https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2024 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Two trillion dollars
what: On 1 March Nvidia closed with a stock market value above two trillion dollars, only the third US company to do so, 180 days after passing one trillion. Technology companies are buying tens of thousands of its H100 chips, which sell for 25,000 to 30,000 dollars each.
why: Apple and Microsoft each took more than 500 days to go from one to two trillion dollars.

title: The most valuable company in the world
what: On 18 June Nvidia's market value passed 3.3 trillion dollars, making it the most valuable company in the world, ahead of Microsoft and Apple. It had closed above 2 trillion dollars for the first time only on 1 March.
why: Twenty-five years after the IPO at a value of a few hundred million dollars.

title: Nvidia joins the Dow, replacing Intel
what: Nvidia was added to the Dow Jones Industrial Average in November, replacing Intel. Morgan Stanley reported that all of next year's production of its new Blackwell chips is already sold out.
why: The changing of the guard in chips.

title: Export licence required for China chips: a 5.5 billion dollar charge
what: On 9 April the US government told Nvidia that it needs a licence to export its H20 chips, designed for the Chinese market, to China, and on 14 April that this applies indefinitely. Nvidia expects charges of up to about 5.5 billion dollars for H20 inventory and purchase commitments.
why: Showed the political risk to Nvidia's China business; in August Nvidia agreed to pay 15% of H20 revenue from China to obtain licences.

title: The first four-trillion-dollar company
what: On 10 July Nvidia became the first company ever to close with a market value above four trillion dollars, worth more than all listed companies in the United Kingdom together.
why: +13% in the month as AI spending kept rising.

title: Five trillion dollars
what: On 29 October Nvidia became the first company to reach a market value of five trillion dollars. In October it agreed a partnership with Nokia on AI in mobile networks and took a stake in the Finnish company; JPMorgan's chief Jamie Dimon warned of a higher chance of a meaningful drop in stocks.
why: The high point so far; the shares moved sideways for the next half year.

title: 68 billion dollars in a quarter
what: Nvidia reported record revenue of 68.1 billion dollars for the quarter to January, 73% more than a year earlier, and net income of about 43 billion dollars, with a gross margin of 75%. At the CES show in January it unveiled its next platform, Vera Rubin.
why: Despite the numbers the shares fell 7% in February.

title: Revenue doubles again: 96 billion dollars a quarter
what: On 26 August Nvidia reported revenue of 96.2 billion dollars for the quarter to July, up 106% from a year earlier, with data-centre revenue of 89.0 billion. Jensen Huang said AI has reached its inflection point and demand is accelerating; its Vera Rubin systems are in full production.
why: The AI boom still accelerating in its fourth year; Nvidia's market value is above five trillion dollars.
